[1] The Pacific Coast League Manager of the Year Award is an annual award given to the best manager in minor league baseball's Pacific Coast League.
[2] John Joseph Lipon (November 10, 1922 – August 17, 1998) was an American Major League Baseball shortstop for the Detroit Tigers, Boston Red Sox, St. Louis Browns and Cincinnati Reds over the course of nine seasons (1942; 1946; 1948–1954).
[3] In 1967, Jack Tighe won the first ever International League Manager of the Year Award.
[4] In 1967, Johnny Lipon won the first ever Pacific Coast League Manager of the Year Award.
